newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-ARBI, HOYER-LARSEN BEATEN IN SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-ARBI, HOYER-LARSEN BEATEN IN SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Indonesia's Heryanto Arbi lost his world badminton crown on Saturday, first tamed and then overwhelmed 9-15 15-9 15-2 by Dane Peter Rasmussen.

But the chance of the first all-Danish men's singles final since 1977 disappeared when Olympic gold medallist Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen was outlasted in the other semifinal by former junior world champion Sun Jun, the Chinese winning 15-7 14-17 15-9.
Rasmussen, 22, represents the new guard for Denmark. Hoyer-Larsen, making his sixth world championship appearance at the age of 31, is of an older school.

Remarkably, in Saturday's matches both Danes trailed 10-0 in their opening games. But while Rasmussen got better and better after the initial nerves, Hoyer-Larsen found Sun the most stubborn of opponents.
Rasmussen hung on and when Arbi was called twice in the second set for service infringements it seemed to unsettle the Indonesian.
Growing in strength and confidence, Rasmussen powered his way to the final with a mixture of heavy, left-handed smashing and some astute tactics.
Rasmussen, seeded 15, said: "I did not expect to win. I have met him twice and lost both matches. I was nervous about his attacking game which is very good."
Arbi, seeded only 12 here after a succession of injuries from mid-1995 saw him slip down the world rankings, looked a tired man at the end.
Hoyer-Larsen, who by his own admission has suffered from post-Olympic euphoria which has prevented him producing his best at tournaments since Atlanta, was totally motivated on Saturday.
Otfen a slow starter, the Dane eventually made a good fist of the first game and looked like he might be gaining the upper hand in the second, although it took seven game points to clinch it.
The effort began to take its toll and 21-year-old Sun, a persistent retriever, finally began to wear down his older opponent.
Hoyer-Larsen said: "My focusing was not good enough. I made too many errors."
The Dane hopes to be around for the 1999 world championships which, it was announced earlier on Saturday, will be in Copenhagen. "It would be nice to win on home ground," he said.
Rasmussen's victory was the only compensation for Denmark who started the day with high hopes.
The pairing of Jens Eriksen and Marlene Thomsen failed gallantly in the mixed doubles final against the powerful Chinese pair of Liu Yong and Ge Fei, who won 15-5 16-17 15-4.
The Chinese had more to celebrate when women's singles titleholder Ye Zhaoying reached the final after beating compatriot Wang Chen 11-5 5-11 11-4.
In Sunday's final she meets another Chinese -- the number two seed Gong Zhichoa who edged past Han Jingna, seeded 10, 12-11 11-9.
The match will be a repeat of March's All-England final, won with embarrassing ease by Ye.
